question: I want a new 'material' field on products that merchants can fill in, and its value should show up on the product detail page in the storefront. What do I need to do in my plugin?
ground_truth: Define a custom field set related to the product entity. Since Shopware 6.7.13.0 this can be declared in <plugin root>/src/Resources/config/custom-fields.xml (a <custom-field-set> with <related-entities><product/></related-entities> and its fields); Shopware creates, updates and removes it during the plugin lifecycle. Before that version, create the set in code with the custom_field_set.repository. Set and field names need a vendor prefix. In the storefront, extend a template such as page/product-detail/description.html.twig with sw_extends, override a block like page_product_detail_description_content_text, call parent() and print {{ page.product.translated.customFields.<field_name> }}, optionally labelled with the automatically created snippet "customFields.<field_name>"|trans|sw_sanitize.

question: I've written an EntityDefinition for my own table. How do I register it so Shopware picks it up, can Shopware generate the CREATE TABLE migration for me, and how do I run that migration?
ground_truth: Register the definition as a service in src/Resources/config/services.php with the shopware.entity.definition tag (e.g. ['entity' => 'swag_example']); getEntityName() must return the table name. With the plugin activated, bin/console dal:migration:create --bundle=<PluginName> --entities=<entity_name> generates a migration containing the CREATE TABLE / ALTER TABLE statements for the definition. Plugin migrations run on install and update; to run new ones by hand use bin/console database:migrate <PluginName> --all. Schema changes belong in update(); updateDestructive() is never run for plugins.

question: I need a background job in my plugin that runs every 10 minutes, but it should only do its work when a checkbox in my plugin's settings is enabled. How do I set this up?
ground_truth: Create a task class extending ScheduledTask with getTaskName() (vendor-prefixed) and getDefaultInterval() returning the interval in seconds (600), and a handler extending ScheduledTaskHandler, marked #[AsMessageHandler(handles: YourTask::class)], whose run() method contains the logic. Register the task in services.php with the shopware.scheduled.task tag and the handler as a message handler. In the handler inject Shopware\Core\System\SystemConfig\SystemConfigService and read the setting with get('<BundleName>.config.<fieldName>') (e.g. SwagBasicExample.config.example), returning early when it is not enabled.

question: I want a new Store API endpoint /store-api/example in my plugin that headless frontends can call, and it must be protected against brute force with a rate limit per IP address. How do I build the route and add the rate limit?
ground_truth: Create an abstract route class (AbstractExampleRoute with getDecorated() and load(Criteria, SalesChannelContext)) and a concrete ExampleRoute extending it with the Store API route scope (#[Route(defaults: [PlatformRequest::ATTRIBUTE_ROUTE_SCOPE => [StoreApiRouteScope::ID]])]) and #[Route(path: '/store-api/example', name: 'store-api.example.search', methods: ['GET','POST'])]; it returns an ExampleRouteResponse extending StoreApiResponse, and the route is registered as a service. For the rate limit create src/Resources/config/rate_limiter.yaml with a unique key (e.g. example_route) and its enabled/policy settings, merge it into the rate limiter configuration with a compiler pass added in the plugin's build() method (PassConfig::TYPE_BEFORE_OPTIMIZATION), inject Shopware\Core\Framework\RateLimiter\RateLimiter into the route and call $this->rateLimiter->ensureAccepted('example_route', $request->getClientIp()), which throws RateLimitExceededException once the limit is exceeded.

question: Sending an SMS from my plugin is slow, so I want it to run in the background instead of during the request. How do I define that job, put it on the queue and write the code that processes it?
ground_truth: Create a message class (e.g. SmsNotification) implementing Shopware\Core\Framework\MessageQueue\AsyncMessageInterface; without it messages are handled synchronously (LowPriorityMessageInterface makes it async with low priority). Dispatch it from a service that gets Symfony\Component\Messenger\MessageBusInterface injected: $this->bus->dispatch(new SmsNotification($content)); an Envelope with a DelayStamp can delay it. Process it in a handler class marked #[AsMessageHandler] with an __invoke(SmsNotification $message) method, registered as a service (messenger.message_handler tag).

question: My plugin has two custom entities: a brand (swag_brand) and its items (swag_item), and each item belongs to exactly one brand. How do I define this relation in both entity definitions, and how do I load a brand together with its items?
ground_truth: The 'many' side (item) gets a foreign key column brand_id: in its definition add an FkField, e.g. new FkField('brand_id', 'brandId', BrandDefinition::class) (column in snake_case, property in lowerCamelCase), and a ManyToOneAssociationField('brand', 'brand_id', BrandDefinition::class, 'id'). The 'one' side (brand) defines a OneToManyAssociationField('items', ItemDefinition::class, 'brand_id'). Autoload defaults to false. To load a brand with its items, add the association to the Criteria with $criteria->addAssociation('items') before searching the brand repository; $criteria->getAssociation('items') lets you filter or limit the loaded items.

question: I want a new storefront page at /example that is rendered by my own controller, and its response should be served from the HTTP cache. How do I set up the controller and make it cacheable?
ground_truth: Create a controller extending StorefrontController with the storefront route scope (#[Route(defaults: [PlatformRequest::ATTRIBUTE_ROUTE_SCOPE => [StorefrontRouteScope::ID]])]) and a #[Route(path: '/example', name: 'frontend.example.example', methods: ['GET'])] action that returns $this->renderStorefront('@SwagBasicExample/storefront/page/example.html.twig', [...]). Register it in services.php as public and call setContainer with the service container, and add a routes.php in src/Resources/config so Shopware loads the plugin's routes. To cache it, add defaults: ['_httpCache' => true] to the route; the HTTP cache then reacts to the logged-in and cart-filled states, and invalidation follows the Store API cache tags of the data loaded.

question: I've built a custom Administration module in my plugin. How do I add it to the admin menu, and make sure only users whose role has the right permission can see the menu entry and open its pages?
ground_truth: Add a navigation array to Shopware.Module.register() with label, color, path, icon, an id and a parent such as 'sw-catalogue' plus position; plugins cannot add first-level menu entries. Register admin privileges with Shopware.Service('privileges').addPrivilegeMappingEntry({ category: 'permissions', parent, key, roles: { viewer: { privileges: ['entity:read', ...], dependencies: [] }, editor: ..., creator: ..., deleter: ... } }). Protect routes by adding meta: { privilege: 'your_key.your_role' } and hide the menu entry by adding privilege: 'your_key.your_role' to the navigation entry.

question: I'm building a custom CMS element for Shopping Experiences that shows a video based on an ID the merchant configures. How do I register the element in the Administration, render it in the Storefront, and load extra data for it on the server side?
ground_truth: In the Administration register it with Shopware.Service('cmsService').registerCmsElement({ name: 'dailymotion', component, configComponent, previewComponent, defaultConfig }) and create the preview, main and config components (imported via main.js). In the Storefront create src/Resources/views/storefront/element/cms-element-<name>.html.twig (prefix cms-element- plus the element name); the element is passed to the template as element. For server-side data create a resolver extending AbstractCmsElementResolver with getType() returning the element name, collect() returning a CriteriaCollection (e.g. for a media ID read via $slot->getFieldConfig()) and enrich() that adds data with $slot->setData(); register it with the shopware.cms.data_resolver tag.

question: My plugin needs its own email template that is installed together with the plugin, and the template has to show some extra data that my plugin computes. How do I add the template and get my data into it?
ground_truth: Add the template in a plugin migration: fetch an existing mail_template_type ID (e.g. technical_name contact_form) or create a custom mail template type, insert a row into mail_template (system_default = 0) and one row per language (e.g. en-GB, de-DE) into mail_template_translation with subject, description and HTML/plain content. Use INSERT IGNORE and do not remove templates on uninstall. To add data, either subscribe to MailBeforeValidateEvent and add template data there, or decorate the MailService (extend AbstractMailService, enrich the $templateData parameter of send() and call the decorated service). The data is then available in the template, e.g. {{ myCustomData }}.

question: My plugin shows text both in the Storefront and in its own Administration module, in English and German. Where do the translation files go in each case, and how do I use them in the templates?
ground_truth: Storefront: put snippet JSON files in <plugin root>/src/Resources/snippet/ named <domain>.<locale>.json (e.g. my-app.en.json, my-app.de.json) with nested keys, and use them in Twig with the trans filter, e.g. {{ 'header.example' | trans }} or with placeholders trans({'%count%': 3}). Administration: create a snippet directory in the module, <plugin root>/src/Resources/app/administration/src/module/<your-module>/snippet/ with en-GB.json and de-DE.json, and use the keys with $tc, e.g. this.$tc('swag-example.general.myCustomText') in JavaScript and $tc(...) in templates (Shopware.Snippet.tc outside components). Clear the cache after adding snippet files.

question: In my payment plugin, how do I create the payment handler, and how can I later change the payment status of the order transaction (for example to paid) and check which status changes are possible at that moment?
ground_truth: Create a handler extending Shopware\Core\Checkout\Payment\Cart\PaymentHandler\AbstractPaymentHandler (the single handler base class since 6.7) and register it in services.php with the shopware.payment.method tag; create a payment method that uses it during plugin install (with a unique technicalName since 6.7). For state changes inject StateMachineRegistry and call transition(new Transition(OrderTransactionDefinition::ENTITY_NAME, $orderTransactionId, 'paid', 'stateId'), $context); the OrderTransactionStateHandler offers helpers such as process(). getAvailableTransitions() on the StateMachineRegistry returns the transitions possible from the current state.

question: I need a bin/console command in my plugin that imports products: it should create a product if it doesn't exist yet and update it if it does. How do I build the command and write the data?
ground_truth: Write a Symfony console command (class extending Command with #[AsCommand(name: 'swag:example')] and an execute() method) and register it in src/Resources/config/services.php with the console.command tag. Inject the product repository (service id product.repository) and call upsert() with an array of product data that includes the id, plus a Context (e.g. Context::createDefaultContext()); upsert updates existing entities and creates missing ones, and without an id it always creates.

question: When my plugin finishes processing one of its example entities, it should fire its own event that carries the sales channel context, and another class in the plugin should react to it. How do I create and dispatch the event, and how do I listen to it?
ground_truth: Create an event class (e.g. ExampleEvent) implementing ShopwareSalesChannelEvent, which provides getContext() and getSalesChannelContext(); pass the entity and the SalesChannelContext through the constructor. Dispatch it from a service that gets Symfony's EventDispatcherInterface injected: $this->eventDispatcher->dispatch(new ExampleEvent($entity, $context)). To react, write a subscriber implementing EventSubscriberInterface whose getSubscribedEvents() maps the event to a method, and register it in services.php with the kernel.event_subscriber tag.

question: When a merchant edits an order, my plugin needs to know which fields changed and, if a certain field changed, set the order's delivery to shipped. How do I get the changed fields and change the delivery state?
ground_truth: Subscribe to OrderEvents::ORDER_WRITTEN_EVENT and ignore versions other than Defaults::LIVE_VERSION. A changeset is not generated by default: also listen to PreWriteValidationEvent and call requestChangeSet() on the relevant write commands, then read $result->getChangeSet() in the written event. To change the delivery state inject StateMachineRegistry and call transition(new Transition(OrderDeliveryDefinition::ENTITY_NAME, $orderDeliveryId, 'ship', 'stateId'), $context), which sets it to shipped.
